english.title: Possess pyrotechnic article at musical event
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) possessed a pyrotechnic article, namely **(..SPECIFY ARTICLE..), when you were at a place

(A)_[where a qualifying musical event, namely **(..SPECIFY THE EVENT..), was being held]_
(B)_[being used by a person responsible for the organisation of a qualifying musical event, namely **(..SPECIFY THE EVENT..), for the purpose of regulation entry to, or departure from, the event or providing sleeping or other facilities for those attending the event]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 134(1) and (3) of the Policing and Crime Act 2017.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) The offence does not apply to organisers of an event or persons having such articles in their possession with the consent of the organisers, see section 134(2) of the Policing and Crime Act 2017.
(ii) 'Qualifying musical events' are specified in regulation 2 of the Policing and Crime Act 2017 (Possession of Pyrotechnic Articles at Musical Events) Regulations 2017.
(iii) For the offence of possession of such articles at football matches, see section 2A of the Sporting Events (Control of Alcohol etc.) Act 1985. Throwing fireworks in public places is an offence under section 80 of the Explosives Act 1875.
